name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::compute_primitive_statistics
behavior: compute_primitive_statistics<T:ArrowNumericType> requires Native:Bounded+PartialOrd, starts min at native maximum and max at native minimum, casts every array to T, sums physical null counts as i64, skips arrays whose entire length is null (including empty arrays), then compares only Some values. all_values_null becomes false upon any non-all-null array. If no valid value exists, return full native [MIN,MAX] and accumulated null count, not null bounds. No checked null-count conversion/sum, mixed-type validation or data concatenation occurs.
callers: get_statistics and get_decimal_statistics.
callees: Arrow primitive casts/iterators, null_count and Native bounds/partial_cmp.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_statistics
behavior: get_statistics<T> debug-asserts nonempty outer input, calls primitive reduction, and constructs nonnull primitive ScalarValues using arrays[0].data_type(), unwrapping both conversions. Using the actual first DataType preserves temporal parameters such as timezone rather than generic T::DATA_TYPE. Later arrays are downcast but no cross-array parameter equality check occurs locally. Empty outer input can panic at first-array indexing even without debug assertions.
callers: collect_statistics integer arms and get_temporal_statistics.
callees: compute_primitive_statistics; ScalarValue::new_primitive with first DataType.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::compute_float_statistics
behavior: compute_float_statistics<T> initializes [+infinity,-infinity], sums physical null counts before skipping all-null/empty arrays, and changes bounds only for strict partial_cmp Greater/Less. NaN comparisons produce no update, but NaNs do not increment null_count. If both sentinels remain unchanged, replace them with [-infinity,+infinity], covering empty, all-null and all-NaN input. Actual single positive or negative infinity updates the opposite bound, preserving a constant-infinity interval.
callers: get_float_statistics.
callees: Arrow primitive casts/iterators, Float infinities/partial_cmp.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_float_statistics
behavior: get_float_statistics uses the float reducer, normalizes any minimum equal to zero to negative zero and any maximum equal to negative zero to positive zero; floating equality covers both zero signs. Converts the resulting native numbers through ScalarValue::from; returns nonnull bounds even for no ordered value. No total-order NaN comparison or timezone/type parameter is involved for Float32/64.
callers: collect_statistics Float32/64 arms.
callees: compute_float_statistics; zero sign normalization; ScalarValue::from.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_decimal_statistics
behavior: get_decimal_statistics reuses Decimal128 native i128 reduction, then reads precision and scale from the first array and wraps both values without precision validation here. No Decimal256 branch exists. Empty/all-null Decimal128 therefore uses native i128 extrema rather than decimal-precision-limited extrema; downstream scalar/Arrow conversion may impose separate constraints, not checked by this reducer.
callers: collect_statistics Decimal128 arm.
callees: compute_primitive_statistics<Decimal128Type>; first-array precision/scale.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::truncate_utf8
behavior: truncate_utf8 asserts data.len()>=length, walks char_indices backward over the original entire string, and returns the longest NONEMPTY valid prefix whose ending byte offset is <=length. It returns None when no full character fits, including length0; it never manufactures Some(empty). The comment says less than length, but actual condition permits equality. Backward traversal may scan the long suffix; the 64-byte comparison limit does not make truncation constant-time in input length. Caller invokes it only for strings longer than64, where at least one Unicode scalar fits.
callers: get_string_statistics.
callees: str::char_indices reverse iteration and byte slicing.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::increment_utf8
behavior: increment_utf8 owns bytes and tries indices right-to-left. For each index it repeatedly increments that byte up to overflow, validating the entire candidate with str::from_utf8 after each attempt; first valid candidate is returned. On exhausting a byte it restores its original value before trying the previous position. Unlike binary carry it does not zero the suffix, change byte length, or construct the next Unicode scalar across multiple changed bytes. A lexically greater same-length valid candidate is conservative; None means this algorithm found none, not a proof that no Unicode upper bound of another form exists. Empty input also returns None.
callers: get_string_statistics.
callees: u8::overflowing_add; str::from_utf8 repeated validation.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::truncate_binary
behavior: truncate_binary asserts input length>=requested length and always returns Some(exact prefix of that length), including zero; there is no all-maximal-byte special case despite the adjacent comment. increment performs big-endian-style carry from the last byte: overflow writes0 and continues left, first nonoverflow returns the same-length vector. All0xFF or empty input returns None. Both less-than comments are imprecise: a prefix may equal the stated length.
callers: get_binary_statistics and get_fixed_size_binary_statistics.
callees: Byte slicing after assertion.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::increment
behavior: truncate_binary asserts input length>=requested length and always returns Some(exact prefix of that length), including zero; there is no all-maximal-byte special case despite the adjacent comment. increment performs big-endian-style carry from the last byte: overflow writes0 and continues left, first nonoverflow returns the same-length vector. All0xFF or empty input returns None. Both less-than comments are imprecise: a prefix may equal the stated length.
callers: get_binary_statistics and get_fixed_size_binary_statistics.
callees: u8::overflowing_add right-to-left carry.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_string_statistics
behavior: get_string_statistics<T:OffsetSizeTrait> casts each array to the chosen UTF8 offset width, accumulates null counts and skips all-null/empty arrays. Each nonnull string longer than64 bytes is truncated at a UTF8 boundary and sets one global bounds_truncated flag. Min/max compare these prefixes lexically with strict comparisons, keeping borrowed references until final ownership conversion. Any truncated value sets the flag even if it never supplies the maximum; short values and empty strings remain eligible. If any string was truncated and a maximum exists, increment_utf8 of the chosen maximum prefix provides the output upper bound; failure turns max into typed None. This also increments a short maximum when a different, smaller value was truncated. Min stays a lower prefix. Borrowed bounds become owned strings; first DataType selects Utf8 versus LargeUtf8, otherwise unreachable. All-null/empty string arrays yield both bounds None, with actual null_count. No truncation means an exact observed maximum, including length exactly64.
callers: collect_statistics UTF8 arms.
callees: Arrow string casts, truncate_utf8, increment_utf8, owned scalar conversion.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_binary_statistics
behavior: get_binary_statistics<T> mirrors string reduction using generic binary casts and raw byte lexicographic ordering. It truncates each value longer than64 to exactly64 bytes, sets a global truncation flag, and compares borrowed slices. Accumulates null counts for every array before skipping all-null/empty arrays. Input consistency is assumed rather than validated. Binary minimum is cloned; maximum is cloned unchanged if no value was truncated, otherwise increment carries through its bytes and can yield None for an all0xFF prefix. The global flag can widen a maximum not itself truncated. First DataType selects Binary or LargeBinary ScalarValue, unmatched type unreachable. Empty/all-null inputs have both typed None; exact64-byte all0xFF remains a present exact maximum when no other value triggers truncation.
callers: collect_statistics Binary arms.
callees: Arrow generic binary casts, truncate_binary, increment.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_fixed_size_binary_statistics
behavior: get_fixed_size_binary_statistics obtains declared width from the first array, sets do_truncate if width>64, then scans nonnull values with lexical byte comparison, truncating each to64 if enabled. Accumulates physical null counts, skips all-null arrays, and assumes common width/type across arrays. Width<=64 compares full values. This helper is callable by the dispatcher but excluded from automatic collector eligibility. Fixed-binary outputs clone the lower prefix and optionally increment the upper prefix on width>64; all-maximal prefix yields None. BOTH ScalarValue::FixedSizeBinary constructors retain the original width, even when present payload has only64 bytes or max is absent. This is a descriptive bound representation, not evidence that those truncated scalar bytes can be appended as valid fixed-width Arrow values. The builder has no fixed-binary append arm (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:918-928).
callers: collect_statistics FixedSizeBinary arm; excluded from automatic collector.
callees: Fixed-size binary cast, truncate_binary, increment, original-width scalar constructors.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_boolean_statistics
behavior: get_boolean_statistics tracks presence of true/false and sums each array null count before an early continue. Once both values have appeared, later arrays need not be scanned for values but still contribute nulls. Within the current array the for_each does not break early. Bounds are Some(true_present&&!false_present) and Some(true_present||!false_present): onlytrue gives true/true, onlyfalse false/false, mixed false/true, no valid values false/true.
callers: collect_statistics Boolean arm.
callees: Boolean casts/iteration; physical null count; presence flags.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::cast_dictionary_arrays
behavior: cast_dictionary_arrays<T> downcasts every dictionary and collects borrowed Arc references to each complete VALUES array into a new Vec. It does not follow keys, deduplicate shared dictionaries, slice values to referenced entries or include key null counts. The returned lifetime is tied to input references.
callers: get_dictionary_statistics.
callees: Dictionary casts and full values() references.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_dictionary_statistics
behavior: get_dictionary_statistics inspects the first Dictionary key type and dispatches Int8/16/32/64 or UInt8/16/32/64 to value extraction, then recursively collect_statistics on those full values arrays. Returned bound scalar type is the dictionary VALUE type. Null count is the sum of values-array null counts, possibly repeatedly counting the same shared dictionary; it is not decoded-row/key null count. Unused dictionary entries affect bounds. Unsupported key type panics naming key type, non-Dictionary call panics naming actual type. This helper remains outside automatic collector selection.
callers: collect_statistics Dictionary arm; excluded from automatic collector.
callees: cast_dictionary_arrays for eight key widths then recursive collect_statistics.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::get_temporal_statistics
behavior: get_temporal_statistics maps Time32 Second/Millisecond, Time64 Microsecond/Nanosecond, Date32/64, all four Timestamp units and all four Duration units to corresponding primitive marker. Timestamp timezone propagates via get_statistics first-array DataType; values are not timezone converted. Other unit/type combinations are unreachable. Native integer extrema supply empty/all-null bounds; temporal domain limits are not validated here.
callers: collect_statistics temporal arms.
callees: get_statistics with selected temporal marker and first dtype parameters.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::collect_statistics
behavior: collect_statistics is pub within the private module and panics with No arrays to collect statistics from on an empty outer slice. It dispatches Boolean, eight integers, Float32/64, temporal families, Decimal128, both binary/string offset widths, FixedSizeBinary and Dictionary based only on the first DataType. Null, Float16, Decimal256, views, structs, lists and other unsupported types reach unreachable; Decimal256 TODO and commented list arms are not support. Returns a row, not Result, and performs no common-type/parameter preflight.
callers: FileWriter::write per selected builder; recursive dictionary reduction and tests.
callees: All typed reducer helpers; panic/unreachable for empty or unsupported inputs.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::supports_stats_collection
behavior: supports_stats_collection is deliberately narrower than collect_statistics: Boolean, eight integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, Utf8/LargeUtf8, Binary/LargeBinary and Decimal128 only. Excludes Time32/64, Timestamp, Duration, Dictionary and FixedSizeBinary despite reducer support; excludes all other unmatched types. FixedSizeBinary is commented out. Do not infer that a dispatcher arm enables on-disk writer statistics.
callers: StatisticsCollector::try_new.
callees: DataType matches whitelist.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::StatisticsCollector::finish
behavior: Collector finish drains each null-count/min/max Arrow builder in ascending ID order, builds Struct children named null_count:Int64 nonnullable and min_value/max_value:original dtype nullable, then a nonnullable root named decimal original field ID. Bounds remain nullable even for a nonnullable data field; null_count builder is appended with nonnull values, and its cloned null buffer supplies root validity. Original Field name/metadata/nullability are not copied to roots. Individual StructArray::new invariants are enforced by Arrow and can panic before the later Result check. Construct RecordBatch using the generated schema/arrays. Any RecordBatch::try_new error is replaced with ArrowError::SchemaError(all columns in a record batch must have the same length), converted to Lance error; original detail is discarded. Builders have already been finished/reset even when this returns Err. No rollback or recovery from prior accumulated rows; caller may collect new rows but cannot retry the old contents. No closed flag prohibits subsequent finish calls.
callers: FileWriter::write_statistics and tests.
callees: ArrayBuilder::finish; StructArray::new; Arrow fields/schema; RecordBatch::try_new and SchemaError replacement.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::visit_fields
behavior: visit_fields creates reversed root stack, pops in schema order, and pushes reversed children ONLY for Struct. It emits the struct node as well as descendants; eligibility later removes structs. Lists, fixed-size lists, dictionaries and other nested types are emitted without descending. This differs from writer fields_in_batches, which emits scalar leaves in reverse root/child traversal order (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:654-692).
callers: StatisticsCollector::try_new.
callees: Reversed root/struct-child stack and DataTypeExt::is_struct.

behavior: new makes a fresh null-count builder and two make_builder(data_type,1) bound builders, retains cloned dtype and returns Self. The1 is initial capacity, not a hard row limit. Arrow make_builder/type support is delegated; collector only calls this for its eligible types.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::StatisticsBuilder::string_statistics_appender
behavior: string_statistics_appender<T> downcasts both bound builders and unwraps before mutation. Appends the supplied i64 null_count with no sign/range check. Utf8 or LargeUtf8 Some values matching self.dt append normally; None OR a mismatched ScalarValue variant appends a null bound instead of an error. Unexpected self.dt is unreachable. Offset-width mismatch panics at downcast.
callers: StatisticsBuilder::append UTF8 arms.
callees: Builder downcasts; append_value/append_null.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::StatisticsBuilder::binary_statistics_appender
behavior: binary_statistics_appender<T> has equivalent behavior for Binary/LargeBinary: checked-by-unwrap builder downcasts, unchecked signed null_count append, matching Some bytes appended and any other ScalarValue mapped to null. It neither truncates nor recomputes statistics; caller supplies row semantics. Unexpected dtype unreachable.
callers: StatisticsBuilder::append binary arms.
callees: Builder downcasts; append_value/append_null.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::StatisticsBuilder::statistics_appender
behavior: statistics_appender<T> downcasts both primitive builders, converts each ScalarValue to a one-element array, unwraps conversion/downcast, and reads raw value(0) without checking validity. Only after both values are obtained does it append count and nonnull min/max. A typed null scalar is not propagated as a null bound; its underlying value is read. Type mismatch or conversion error panics. Scalar type parameters are not independently compared with self.dt.
callers: StatisticsBuilder::append primitive/temporal/decimal arms.
callees: Builder downcasts; ScalarValue::to_array; PrimitiveArray::value(0); nonnull append.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::StatisticsBuilder::boolean_appender
behavior: boolean_appender downcasts both Boolean builders, appends count, then matching Some Boolean bounds; absent or wrong-variant minimum becomes false and maximum becomes true. It never emits a null Boolean bound. This fallback differs from string/binary null insertion and primitive raw value extraction.
callers: StatisticsBuilder::append Boolean arm.
callees: BooleanBuilder downcasts and false/true fallback.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::StatisticsBuilder::append
behavior: append matches stored dt, routing Boolean, eight integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, supported Time32/64 units, all four Timestamp and Duration units and Decimal128 to the corresponding appender. Temporal branches exist even though automatic collector filters them out. No row type/count validation or error-return channel precedes dispatch. Append handles Binary/LargeBinary and Utf8/LargeUtf8 with correct offset marker. Decimal256 remains TODO, Dictionary has a comment that stats concern values but no dictionary branch, and FixedSizeBinary also has no branch. Everything else executes todo!(Stats collection for {} is not supported yet). End of builder impl; no persisted format is directly emitted here.
callers: FileWriter::write and local tests.
callees: Type-selected primitive, Boolean, string or binary appender; todo! for unsupported dtype.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::tests::test_collect_primitive_stats
behavior: test_collect_primitive_stats private TestCase stores source arrays, expected min/max and expected i64 count. First8 of24 cases test Int8/16/32/64 using [4,3,7,2] plus [-10,3,5] ->[-10,7], and UInt8/16/32/64 using [4,3,7,2] plus [10,3,5] ->[2,10]. Every expected count is0, with exact matching scalar width. Primitive cases9-15 cover Boolean [true,false] ->[false,true]; Date32/Date64 and Time32 Second/Millisecond, Time64 Microsecond/Nanosecond each use [53,42] plus [68,32] ->[32,68] with the corresponding scalar variant and count0. No temporal range validation or null entries are tested. Four Timestamp cases use each unit Second/Millisecond/Microsecond/Nanosecond on [53,42] plus [68,32], explicitly attach UTC to both arrays, and expect same-unit UTC ScalarValues32/68 with count0. They check metadata propagation, not timezone conversion or mismatched zones. Final primitive cases cover four Duration units with the same32/68 bounds/count0; Decimal128 arrays are constructed from [53,42] and [68,32] and expected scalars are explicitly try_new_decimal128(32 or68,38,10). No explicit with_precision_and_scale is applied to source arrays here; dependency defaults/equality are not independently validated by this source-reading task. Iterate all24 cases, borrow each ArrayRef, collect and compare complete StatisticsRow with expected bounds/count, including input arrays in assertion failure text. No collector builder or file serialization is involved.
callers: Rust/proptest test discovery; read, not executed.
callees: Concrete Arrow fixtures, collect_statistics/collector methods, and exact assertions in cited ranges.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::writer::statistics::tests::test_stats_collector
behavior: test_stats_collector builds nullable a:Int32,b:Utf8 schema. Append two rows to a only: count2 bounds1..3 then count0 boundsi32MIN..MAX. finish is asserted is_err because b has zero rows; no error variant/message check. Comment correctly warns finished builders lost prior rows; test constructs a new collector instead of retrying old contents. Recreated collector appends same two a rows, then b count6 aaa..bbb and count0 typed None/None. Successful finish must have roots named0/1 in ID order, each nonnullable Struct with nonnullable Int64 null_count and nullable correctly typed bounds. Exact schema equality asserted; original names a/b are absent. Build complete expected two-row batch: root0 null counts[2,0],min[1,i32MIN],max[3,i32MAX]; root1 counts[6,0],min[aaa,null],max[bbb,null]. All structs are valid and both Arrow root/bound types match expected schema. Assert full RecordBatch equality, not just schema or min/max extrema. Second collector fixture uses Boolean,Binary,LargeBinary,Utf8,LargeUtf8 roots with IDs0..4. Appends one row each,count0; Boolean boundsfalse/true and all four string/binary variants typed None/None. These rows are manually supplied, not derived from input arrays. Expected five-root schema spells decimal names0..4 with nonnullable Struct/null_count and nullable min/max in Boolean,Binary,LargeBinary,Utf8,LargeUtf8 respectively. The schema declaration verifies type and nullability preservation, not automatic eligibility of other types. Expected one-row batch starts roots0..2: each count[0]; Boolean min[false]/max[true], Binary and LargeBinary both single null bounds. Uses separate StructArrays and Arc child fields. No root nulls are introduced. Expected roots3/4 use cloned one-element None string vector in StringArray and LargeStringArray; counts[0]. finish actual collector and assert both schema equality and entire batch equality. End of deterministic collector test; it does not test duplicate IDs, empty eligible schema, parent validity or post-finish retry.
